instruction.text: Select the arm to place three leeches on it.

feedback.finish: In the Middle Ages, if people thought you had too much blood, they would use leeches to suck some of it away. In fact, this was a common treatment until as late as the 1800s!

instruction.text: Find all the things that would have spread illness in this town.

feedback.correct: Butchers would sometimes throw away bad meat, which attracted rats.
Many cities had toilets, but lazy people might just throw their waste into the streets with buckets.
If dirt and germs got into the water people drank and washed with, they could get very ill.

text.text: To help with cleaning up, cities hired people called gongfermers, whose job was to move sewage out of the city. Essentially, they were poo collectors!

instruction.text: Medieval medicine in Western Europe was heavily affected by the Church. Decide whether these things were helpful or harmful.

sound.start: The church offered free care to the poor
Monks copied down historic texts to help people learn.
Doctors were discouraged from having new ideas and followed ancient practices instead.
The church sometimes would suggest praying for a cure rather than using medicine.

atoms.b: During this time, the Islamic kingdoms were making a lot of ((++medical magical)) and scientific advancements.
While the English Church only copied certain ((++texts films)) that they approved of, the Islamic kingdoms copied everything they could find, and put them in public ((++libraries zoos)).
Many European peasants were not able to ((++read speak)), but most people in the Arab world were literate because Muslims were encouraged to read the ((++Qur’an Bible)).

hint.label: Literate
hint.text: You are literate if you are able to read and write.

atoms.b: The focus on ((++education elephants)) meant that the Islamic kingdoms had a lot of good scientists. This is Al-Razi, a doctor who built the first ever general ((++hospital helicopter)) in Baghdad in the year 805 AD.
